1. LEGAL PINCHING AND EXACT RIGHT-MODULUS MASS

Let H=direct_sum_lambda H_lambda be finite and let every target rho_x be
block diagonal. Its full trace-one mean sigma>0 is block diagonal. Consider
any CPTP reconstruction through maximum conditional quantum dimension Q.
Input sector pinching fixes every actual input and does not raise maximum
branch Q. Thus a competing channel can legally be replaced by this INPUT-
pinched one. Output pinching is legal too, but is not needed here.

Refine its rank-Q Kraus operators by the input projectors,

  A_(i,mu)=A_i P_mu, B_(i,mu)=A_(i,mu)sqrt(sigma).

These represent the input-pinched channel with rank<=Q. B has source
H_mu and output range anywhere in H. Right moduli are supported on mu;
left moduli may cross output sectors, and are only used in the paired
nonnegative energy inequality. For ANY chosen source subset C define the
positive selected terms

  F_z=|B_(i,mu)|/sqrt(2), mu in C.

Then rank F_z<=Q, each F_z is supported on one source sector, and

  sum_z F_z^2=sigma P_C/2,
  sum_z||F_z||_HS^2=(1/2)Tr sigma P_C.                 (1.1)

Proof: sum B^dag B=sigma by TP, and |B|^2=B^dag B. Sum its source columns
over mu in C. This is exact even when the decoder always changes the sector,
the sector weights are unequal, or Phi(sigma) has zero output sectors.
The F_z need not define a TP map; they are positive matrices in a converse.
No source state or outcome is discarded from the experiment.

2. SIMULTANEOUS ENERGY DOMINATION

For any Hermitian field H_x on H, the exact SVD inequality is

  [||[H_x,|B|]||_HS^2+||[H_x,|B^dag|]||_HS^2]/2
                                           <=||[H_x,B]||_HS^2.

Therefore selection of nonnegative right terms gives

  sum_z int||[H_x,F_z]||_HS^2
                         <=sum_(i,mu)int||[H_x,B_(i,mu)]||_HS^2. (2.1)

The RHS indexes the FULL REFINED input-pinched Kraus list
B_(i,mu)=A_i P_mu sqrt(sigma). For a wholly arbitrary non-block-diagonal
Hermitian H_x it is not identified with the original unrefined Kraus
energy. The operational fields used in the iid application are block
diagonal, but the abstract inequality above keeps its exact refined index.

The SAME selected F_z satisfies (1.1),(2.1) for any finite collection of
Hermitian score fields simultaneously. Keeping all right moduli alone
would have exact source mass but need not decrease energy. Energy-favorable
orientations
